sonnet.problem: The card pulls Isaiah 40:19-20 (the idol passage from the preceding chapter) into a full sentence. This implies the thing being welded in 41:7 is an idol, which 41:7 never says. The prior passage is context only, and the text leaves open what the craftsmen are making.
sonnet.rule: An outside passage, like a New Testament fulfillment, only rides along in a few words on a card that tells this passage.

sonnet.problem: The verses are a promise ("I will make you…", "You will thresh…"), but the card tells it in the present tense: "it threshes the mountains and turns the hills to chaff."
sonnet.rule: A prediction stays a prediction: "God says Tyre will fall," never "Tyre falls."

sonnet.problem: The question states a promised future event as happening now: "A wind carries the chaff away and a gale scatters it." The text says a wind will carry them away and a gale will scatter them.
sonnet.rule: A prediction stays a prediction: "God says Tyre will fall," never "Tyre falls."
